subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed native subagent startup failures stay in the accepted async run contract with a terminal `startup-failed` state, or should `sessions_spawn` preflight sandbox startup before returning accepted?
rationale: Both shapes can address the silent hang, but the choice affects gateway accepted semantics, child session registry state, lifecycle events, and the overlapping #58776/#77415 design.

options.title: Terminalize async startup failure
options.body: Keep the accepted spawn contract, then emit and persist a typed startup failure with live Docker proof that callers see the child run fail visibly.

options.title: Preflight before accepted
options.body: Move enough sandbox startup validation ahead of the accepted response, accepting added latency and compatibility implications for existing callers.

options.title: Defer to lifecycle PR
options.body: Block this issue on a corrected lifecycle PR and use #39248 as the required Docker-specific proof case before closure.

recommendation.title: Terminalize async startup failure
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted spawn contract, then emit and persist a typed startup failure with live Docker proof that callers see the child run fail visibly.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the broadest observed history across sessions_spawn sandbox inheritance, sandbox backends, and subagent lifecycle seams.
